messages.subject: Getting unusual fitted values in a simple model
messages.subject_clean: Getting unusual fitted values in a simple model
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Currently I am trying to fit a spatial-temporal model with count data in inla with data over a five year period. When fitting a simple model with only a besag spatial term and no temporal terms, I checked the fitted values for each year at the first location to check if they were all the same but they were slightly different at each year. The fitted values from the inla model were only different by a few decimal places for each year at each area but should have all been the same as it would have been using the same intercept and spatial term for that specific area. The spatial terms were the same value at each area over the five year period so I am unsure of what might be causing these strange fitted values.

This model also an unusual warning message that did not appear with other models fitted with inla that had more than one term in them. Any ideas on what might be causing this?

Here is the code and warning given
formula1 <-  y ~ f(NO, model="besag", graph = W)
 inla(formula1, family="poisson",data=data, control.compute=list(dic=1))

*** Warning *** Numerical error gives b22 = -17298.6 <= 0.0 for idx=1626. setting b22=1.49167e-154
*** Warning *** Numerical error gives b22 = -73990.9 <= 0.0 for idx=1626. setting b22=1.49167e-154

Craig

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Combine inla.stack and inla.make.lincombs?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Annette,

this might be possible, by using and A-matrix (e.g. from
inla.stack.A(...) or directly from inla.spde.make.A(...) ), but how
easy it would be depends on your model structure, I believe.  The
weights in make.lincombs apply to the effects themselves, whereas the
stack-A is applied to the linear predictor, so they don't mean the
same thing, so you might have to replicate your inla.stack call with a
similar inla.make.lincombs call.

inla.stack can partly be seen as a different way of building lincombs,
and ideally the internal handling of prediction using weight
specifications from inla.stack and inla.make.lincombs would work the
same, but that is not the case, due to the implementation history of
the two features.  Hopefully they can be merged in the future.

/Finn

messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I have a set of LAT-LONG and utilizing a methodology similar to the Blangiardo spde spatial model, with the hope of progressing to a spatio-temporal model.

As far as what I have read in the papers and the discussion group I have two options

1) Convert lat-long to UMTX and UMTY
2) Convert lat-long to 3d Cartesian XYZ

It seems that you favor method 2 so that is what I am sticking with. I was hoping you could give me ideas how to plot the mesh resulting from my R3 specification to check that my borders etc are correct.

Thanks for any assistance

Sam

My problem with this is, only when I close this window by hand, my loop
computing inla results for several prediction days, contiues, otherwise the
function is hovering at the current loop step as the inla call of the
current step is not finished/terminated or whatever.
Is there any possibilty
either to prevent this inla.exe crashes in general or in somehow give the
inla call an argument so that this windows 7 "information window" does not appear but that in case of inla.exe crashing the current inla call is just
stopped/terminated so that my loop can continue to the next step and try the next inla call?
This problem with this windows 7 window is really annoying,
as I always need to stop it by hand and cannot just run the whole loop
without interacting several times. It is ok when inla crashes at some steps
and I have a NULL result there, thats not the main problem (although of course it would be best if inla always finishes.. ;-) ), but it takes very long time if I always have
to check if there is this crashing-window and then close it by hand...

Thanks,
Annette

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] plot R3 to S2
messages.body_plain:
Which model domain is preferred for geographical coordinates depends
on the size of the domain.  If the region is small enough, UMTX/UTMY
should be fine, but if the domain is large enough to "notice" the
curvature of the globe, using the sphere itself (or a subset) gives
correct distances.

To plot spherical fields (or part-spherical in your case, as far as I
understand), the same inla.mesh.project/or methods can be used as for
planar meshes.  The documentation for that has unfortunately lagged
behind a bit...

Available projections is sphere-->long&lat-grid (projection="longlat),
sphere-->long&sin(lat) (projection="longsinlat"; this is an equal-area
projection), the mollweide projection (projection="mollweide"; this is
also equal are, but with less shape distortion), and also any
projection defined by points of your own choosing, such as a grid in
UMTX/Y (which you first have to project onto XYZ on the sphere).

You can also produce a 3d-plot use rgl using some old functionality.
Off the top off my head, I think
  plot(old.mesh.class(mesh),col=somevalues)
should do the trick.

/Finn

messages.subject: Measurement error model in INLA
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

I am trying to use R-INLA for a measurement error problem. However, I am struggling to formulate it properly, so I would appreciate any help you could give.

The model is something like this:

log(y) = a + b*log(x)

However, we don't have measurements of x itself. Instead, we have 3 approximations of x with error (w). So w_i = x + eps_i.

So this is a basic measurement error problem. The only additional complexity is that both y and x are count data.

I would like to simultaneously estimate x and then use that estimate in the equation above to calculate a and b

My first thought was to use the copy function. I defined the formula as

formula = cbind(x, y)~ 0 + trt + f(j, model='iid', hyper=list(theta=list(fixed=FALSE))) +
                    f(j2, copy='j', hyper=list(theta=list(fixed=FALSE))),

where j and j2 are indices for the replicates of x and y, and are NA when x and y are NA. trt is a label for whether each datapoint is an x or a y.

The problem I see here is that  I think this is fitting the equation
log(y) = a + b*log(v)
where v[j] = log(x[j]) - mean(log(x))

Is there anyway of fitting this sort of model in inla? It seems like something it could do, but I can't figure it out. My knowledge of the tools to manipulate models is still fairly poor. Apologies if this is trivial.

I have code that simulates sthe sort of data we have (it's a little more complex than the description above, but not much). I have attached this in case it is useful.

Many thanks in advance for any help.

best wishes
Robi

## Below is a simulation of the type of data we have.

## There are 3 measurements of x, w_i (i=1:3) for each of 36 replicates,(j=1:36)

## For each replicate, we measured y under k treatments to provide y_jk.
## For simplicities sake, let us assume that k = 2,

## I  have simulated different effects of density under the two treatments
## For one, x has no effect (b=1) but for the other x as a strongeffect (b=0.8)

## here is the simulation:
## a function that takes lambda, the expecation of x,
## also a and b to simulate y data
## this simulates x_i and y_i
## Note that x_i for another call of sdlgen with the same
## lambda will give a 'measurement' of x, called w_i
sdlgen <- function(lambda, a, b, model='nb'){
  ## (default) negative binomial with parameters size=1, p=1/(1+lambda)
  if(model=='nb')
    n0=rnbinom(n=length(lambda), mu=lambda, size=1)  ## simulated x_ij
  else
    ## otherwise poisson with parameters lambda=lambda
    n0=rpois(n=length(lambda), lambda)

  ## now simulate y as y_ij = a*x_ij^b
  n1 <- rbinom(length(lambda), size=n0, prob=a*n0^(b-1))
  return(cbind(n0,n1))                  # return both the N0 and the N1
}
## set parameters for the simulation
a <- 0.1; b1 <- 1; b2 <- 0.8 ## b=effect of x
                                        # b1 and b2 are two treatments,
                                        # b1 has no effect,
                                        # b2 has a small one
j <- 1:36                ## vector of replicates, j
lambda <- exp(rnorm(36, mean=5)) ## expected x for each station, lambda_j;

## looking at the expected curves
curve(a*x^b1, from=1, to=1000)
curve(a*x^b2, from=1, to=1000, add=T, lty=2) ## note b2 gives lower y at high x

## now simulate the "observed" data
## simulate x 3 times to get w_ij
## note for w_ij we take the n0 instead of n1 from the simulations
w <- Reduce(function(x, y) return(c(x, y)),
            x=replicate(3, sdlgen(lambda=lambda, a=1, b=1)[,'n0'], simplify=F))

y1 <- sdlgen(lambda=lambda, a=a, b=b.a)  ## first y, with NO effect of x
y2 <- sdlgen(lambda=lambda, a=a, b=b.c) ## second y with effect of x
colnames(y1) <- c('x1', 'y1') ## note we keep the 'real' x for comparison
colnames(y2) <- c('x2', 'y2')
## overplot these on the curves
points(y1, pch=1)
points(y2, pch=2)

## put all the data into a dataframe for analysis with INLA - padding with NAs as appropriate
dat.t <- data.frame(j=rep(j, 5), lambda=rep(lambda, 5),
                    trt=factor(c(rep('w', 36*3), rep('y1', 36), rep('y2', 36)),
                      levels=c('w', 'y1', 'y2')),
                    w=c(w, rep(NA, 36*2)),
                    y1=c(rep(NA, 36*3), y1[,2], rep(NA, 36)),
                    y2=c(rep(NA, 36*4), y2[,2]))
## NOTE trt=T: the seeds in adjacent seed traps (3 per station, j)
##      trt=A: recruits in seedling plots when there is no effect of density (1 per station, j)
##      trt=C: recruits in seedling plots when there is  (1 per station, j)

dat.t$j1 <- c(rep(j, 3), rep(NA, 36*2))     ## index for replicate for w
dat.t$j2 <- c(rep(NA, 36*3), j, rep(NA, 36)) ## index for replicate for trt 1
dat.t$j3 <- c(rep(NA, 36*3), rep(NA, 36), j) ## index for replicate for trt 2

## Now fit the (wrong in this case) model
library(INLA)

m.inla <- inla(cbind(w, y1, y2)~trt + f(j1, model='iid', hyper=list(theta=list(fixed=F))) +
                      f(j2, copy='j1', hyper=list(theta=list(fixed=FALSE))) +
                      f(j3, copy='j1', hyper=list(theta=list(fixed=FALSE))),
                      family=rep('nbinomial', 3), data=dat.t,  control.compute=list(dic=TRUE))
m.inla$summary.hyper

messages.subject: inconsistent results from bivariate model (2diid)
messages.body_plain:
Dear INLA Forum,

I am having trouble with retrieving known parameter values from
simulated data sets using a bivariate model after the
BivariateMeta.code (
http://www.r-inla.org/examples/volume-ii/code-for-model-bivariatemetaanalysis
). I would expect consistency with large sample size, which obviously
does not happen in this case. Could anyone please tell me how to fix
the code so that I can get the parameter values right?

library(MASS)
library(INLA)
library(dclone)

## Bivariate Binomial model simulation -- no fixed effects
n <- 1000
g <- 1:n
N <- 100 # trials

sig1 <- 0.8
sig2 <- 1.2
rho <- -0.8

Sig <- matrix(0, 2, 2)
Sig[1,1] <- sig1^2
Sig[2,2] <- sig2^2
Sig[1,2] <- sig1*sig2*rho
Sig[2,1] <- Sig[1,2]

E <- mvrnorm(length(unique(g)), c(0,0), Sig)[g,]
y <- rbinom(n, N, plogis(E))

f <- y ~ f(g, model="2diid", n=n*2) - 1
m <- inla(f, family="binomial", data=data.frame(y=y, g=dclone(dciid(g), 2),
    Ntr=rep(N,2*n)), Ntrials=Ntr)
summary(m)
re <- m$summary.hyperpar[,1]
cbind(truth=c(sig1=sig1,sig2=sig2,rho=rho),
    estimate=c(sqrt(1/re[1]),sqrt(1/re[2]),re[3]))

And here is what I get (Win 7, R 2.15.2).

     truth   estimate
sig1   0.8 0.73138017
sig2   1.2 0.65320799
rho   -0.8 0.09161783

Thanks in advance,

Peter

messages.body_plain:
On Thu, 2012-12-13 at 09:34 -0700, Peter Solymos wrot

Hi, the main error is to assume that

> y <- rbinom(n, N, plogis(E))

returns a nx2 matrix of y's if plogis(E) is that, but rbinom only use
the first column of plogis(E), so it has to go wrong.

> f <- y ~ f(g, model="2diid", n=n*2) - 1

the '2diid' model is an old one and the newer is 'iid2d'. the difference
is in the prior spesifiction, and generally, we recommend to use the
'iid2d' model; see inla.doc("iid2d")

I attach modified code, which gave (randomly) these results for n=1000,

> cbind(truth=c(sig1=sig1,sig2=sig2,rho=rho),
+     estimate=c(sqrt(1/re[1]),sqrt(1/re[2]),re[3]))
     truth      estimate
sig1   0.8  0.7880554811
sig2   1.2  1.2243833575
rho   -0.8 -0.8012335005

Best
H

--
INLA help <he...@r-inla.org>

I think the formula is what you want. the besag model for a lattice is
not implemented but for a general graph it is.

Here is how to generate a graph-file for a regular lattice with Rows and
Columns:

> R = toeplitz(c(1,1,0,0,0,0,0))
> C = toeplitz(c(1,1,0,0))
> Q = kronecker(R,C)
> inla.spy(Q)
> graph = inla.read.graph(Q)
> inla.write.graph(graph, filename="graph.txt", mode="ascii")

H

messages.subject: Re: Measurement error model in INLA
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,
Since I first sent this mail, Håvard has given me a lot of help off-list on this topic. A model can be defined in INLA to address this sort of analysis, but first a redefinition of the problem might be helpful as my initial post was a little confusing.

we assume that x is unobserved but w is and is related to x by

w ~ Pois(exp(x))

However, we are primarily interested in the relationship between x and another variable poisson distributed variable y, and want to fit

log(y) = a + bx
so
y ~ Pois(exp(a + bx))

The model is then easily fitted with the following code from Håvard:

## estimate 'a' and 'b'
## w ~ Pois(exp(x))
## y ~ Pois(exp(a + b*x))

n = 1000
x = rnorm(n)
a = 1.1
b = 2.2

w = rpois(n,  lambda = exp(x))
y = rpois(n,  lambda = exp(a + b*x))

Y = c(w, y)
X = c(1:n, rep(NA, n))
XX = c(rep(NA, n), 1:n)
A = c(rep(NA, n), rep(1, n))

formula = Y ~ -1 + A +
    f(X, model="iid") +
    f(XX, copy="X", hyper = list(theta = list(fixed=FALSE)))

r = inla(formula,
        data = data.frame(Y, X, XX, A),
        family = "poisson")
summary(r)

This works beautifully, giving good estimates of w, a and b. Thanks to Håvard for all the help,

Hope this is useful to someone. I'm happy to share the code for a more complex simulation with anyone who is interested.

Best wishes
Robi
